message.reasoning:
Two claims: A: serum irisin positively correlated with HbA1c in entire study group (FPLD2, OND, HC). B: plasma irisin negatively correlated with glycated hemoglobin (r=-0.283, p=0.024).

Both are correlation analyses of irisin vs HbA1c/glycated hemoglobin. Same exposure type (irisin, serum vs plasma — similar biomarker measurement), same outcome (HbA1c/glycated hemoglobin). Directions are opposite: + vs -. Genuinely opposite findings.

Check extraction correctness: A's claim matches sentence 10. B's claim matches sentence 9. Both correct.

Comparability: different populations (lipodystrophy/obese/controls vs Brazilian surgical patients by BMI), serum vs plasma, but both correlation of irisin with HbA1c. Comparable contrast. Opposite directions.

Apparent contradiction: is there a text-supported contextual difference? A's population includes FPLD2 patients with insulin resistance and higher irisin; B's population is obesity spectrum with different irisin behavior. The abstracts describe different populations: A is a case-control study of FPLD2, OND, HC; B is a cohort of patients stratified by BMI undergoing surgery. Is that a "concrete, relevant contextual difference that could explain" the opposite correlation? The populations differ substantially — A includes lipodystrophy patients characterized by insulin resistance with high irisin; B suggests irisin inversely correlates with insulin resistance states. The population difference is text-supported: A sentence 4 (19 FPLD2, 13 OND, 19 HC), B sentence 3 (BMI-stratified groups). Also sample type: serum vs plasma — that's a measurement difference but probably not explanatory of direction.

Is population difference sufficient as explanatory? The instructions say don't invent explanations; different populations alone... "Different sample sizes alone are not automatically explanatory." Population composition difference is a concrete difference. In A, the positive correlation is driven partly by FPLD2 patients with high irisin and high HbA1c (insulin resistance). In B, negative correlation in obese patients. The abstracts each describe their own population; the difference in study populations (rare lipodystrophy vs obesity spectrum) is a plausible text-supported explanation. I think apparent_contradiction with factor "population" is appropriate. Enumerated main factor — likely "population" is one of the enumerated factors (population, intervention/exposure, outcome, comparison type, statistical analysis, other, none, unknown). Use population.

Alternatively contradictory/none. But the populations are quite different: A includes FPLD2 (lipoatrophy with muscle hypertrophy) where irisin correlates with lean mass; B is general obesity. The abstracts support this difference. I'll go with apparent_contradiction, factor population.

Rationale: A reports positive correlation of serum irisin with HbA1c in a case-control set including FPLD2; B reports negative correlation (r=-0.283, p=0.024) in BMI-stratified surgical cohort. Text-supported difference: A's population includes FPLD2 with insulin resistance and higher lean mass; B's cohort is obesity-stratified patients. Cite quotes from both.

source_evidence.quote: In the entire study group, irisin levels positively correlated with BMI, lean body mass and index, intra-abdominal/total abdominal fat ratio, triglyceride, cholesterol, insulin, glucose and HbA1c levels.

Irisin was negatively correlated with weight (r = -0.246; p = 0.042), waist circumference (r = -0.272; p = 0.024), glucose (r = -0.259; p = 0.039), glycated hemoglobin (r = -0.283; p = 0.024), triglycerides (r = -0.414; p = 0.024), and positively correlated with HDL (r = 0.280; p = 0.029).

verdict.label: apparent_contradiction
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report a correlation between circulating irisin and HbA1c/glycated hemoglobin, but with opposite directions: study A reports a positive correlation in the entire study group (sentence 10), while study B reports a negative correlation (r = -0.283; p = 0.024, sentence 9). The abstracts describe concrete, different study populations that could explain this: A is a case-control study of LMNA-associated partial lipodystrophy (FPLD2) with obese non-diabetic patients and healthy controls, in which irisin is increased in FPLD2/OND and correlates with lean body mass and insulin-resistance markers (sentences 4, 8, 10, 12); B is a prospective cohort of BMI-stratified surgical patients in Southern Brazil in which irisin inversely tracks weight and glycemic measures (sentences 2-3, 9-10). This text-supported population difference supports apparent_contradiction rather than contradictory; neither abstract discusses the other's setting, and no claim of clinical truth or treatment is made.
